newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends lower, central bank steps in.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends lower, central bank steps in.

text.p: Despite dollar supply from the central Bank of Korea (BOK), the won closed lower against the U.S. unit in tight-range trading on Friday, dealers said.
The won closed at 874.90, compared with Thursday's close of 874.40. It opened at a new 84-month low of 875.00.
Dealers said BOK began selling dollars from the opening. But BOK has refused to confirm or deny intervention talk.
"There was strong resistance around the 875.00 won level, leaving the market moving in very narrow range," said a foreign bank dealer.
Dealers said an estimated $500 million was sold by the central bank, accounting for more than 60 percent of Friday's trading volume.
They said the central bank also offered to sell $20 million at the 888.00 won level in three-month forward trading.

"The BOK is the only dollar supplier," said a local bank dealer. "But the greenback is expected to test the 880.00 won level next week, if the dollar's strength continues in global financial markets."
Dealers forecast Monday's mid-rate would be fixed at 875.00 against 874.00 today. -- Yeom Yoon-jeong (822) 727 5647
